extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and research support staff preparing ERC Starting or Consolidator Grant applications (2024)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant proposals in the 2024 calls, including eligibility, proposal structure, CV/track-record expectations, evaluation questions and process, panel selection, and resubmission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator profile (StG vs CoG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grant: already evidence of potential for research independence. Consolidator Grant: already evidence of research independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PI profile to justify which call (StG or CoG) you apply to; demonstrate potential vs established independence through outputs, leadership of projects, supervision, and other indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Host must be in an EU Member State or an Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure host organisation commitment (Letter of Support) and that the PI's physical commitment meets EU/Associated Country presence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum research time commitment thresholds: StG ≥ 50% (and ≥ 50% in Europe); CoG ≥ 40% (and ≥ 50% in Europe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare and justify the percentage commitment in the Resources & time commitment section and ensure host supports this commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding caps and additional funding justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum funding: StG max. €1.5 million (5 years); CoG max. €2 million (5 years). Additional funding up to €1 million possible with special justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request additional funding only with a clear special justification (e.g., major equipment, access to research infrastructures, major experimental/field work). Explain necessity and cost basis in the proposal budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: New CV & track record template expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: New template requires: research achievements (≤10) showing advancement in the field with short narratives on significance and emphasis on recent achievements; peer recognition (prizes, fellowships, academy membership); career breaks, diverse career paths, and contributions to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select up to 10 achievements that best demonstrate scientific quality and impact; provide concise narratives explaining significance; document career interruptions and diverse trajectories transparently; include indicators of peer recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation focus on the proposed research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased focus on the proposed research: ground‑breaking nature, ambition, potential impact, and feasibility are emphasised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the scientific proposal to highlight novelty, transformative potential and ambitious objectives while providing credible feasibility and risk mitigation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined evaluation questions (what reviewers will ask)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key evaluation questions include: To what extent is the proposed research high risk–high gain and are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art? Is the scientific approach feasible given the ground‑breaking nature and ambition? Does the PI provide evidence of creative, independent and original thinking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these questions explicitly in the proposal narrative: articulate ambition and beyond‑state‑of‑the‑art aspects, acknowledge and argue feasibility given high risk, and provide concrete evidence of independent creativity in the PI track record and project plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal structure and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Required parts and page limits: B1 administrative forms (online); Extended synopsis (B1) 5 pages; CV & track record 4 pages; B2 Scientific proposal 14 pages; Resources & time commitment 2 pages. Supporting documents: Host Letter of Support, PhD certificate (and supporting documentation), ethics issues table if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the page limits strictly; allocate content to the correct sections (short summary in B1, full scientific case in B2). Include mandatory supporting documents and ensure certificates and host letters are current and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window based on PhD defence (reference date 1 Jan 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grant: >2 and ≤7 years prior to 1 Jan 2024 (PhD defense between 1 Jan 2017 and 31 Dec 2021). Consolidator Grant: >7 and ≤12 years prior to 1 Jan 2024 (defense between 1 Jan 2012 and 31 Dec 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check your PhD defence date against the call cut‑off dates; calculate eligibility carefully and provide documentary proof (PhD certificate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of eligibility period (allowable documented interruptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions beyond the standard windows may be granted for: maternity leave (18 months per child, before/after PhD), paternity leave (documented), national military/civil service (after defence), long‑term illness (>90 days) of PI or close family member (after PhD), clinical training (after reference date, up to 4 years), inability to work due to natural disaster, inability to work due to seeking asylum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and justify each requested extension with dates and supporting evidence; apply the prescribed months/years per type of interruption as stated by the Work Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD equivalency rules for medical degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: For medical degrees the eligibility window is shifted: use the certified date of medical degree completion (reference in Germany: 3rd Staatsexamen) plus two years → eligibility windows become 4–9 years (StG) or 9–14 years (CoG). Proof may include appointment that requires doctoral equivalency and evidence of research qualification (peer‑reviewed publications). For PIs with both medical degree and PhD, the earliest degree that makes the PI eligible is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold a medical degree, provide the certified completion date and any required proof of research qualification or appointment to claim the adjusted window; if holding multiple degrees, state which date is used for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process and stages (including interview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process: Submission of full proposals → Eligibility check → Step 1 (remote) evaluation of Part B1 by panel members → 1st Panel meeting → Individual assessment of full proposal (B1 + B2) by panel members & referees → 2nd Panel meeting with INTERVIEW of applicants → Panel chairs’ meeting and consolidation of 3 domain rank lists → Selection of proposals passing to Step 2 → Proposals selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for both written assessment and an interview; ensure B1 and B2 are consistent and that the Extended synopsis can be used in Step 1 remote evaluations; plan materials and presentation for the interview stage if shortlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer‑review composition and role of remote experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is conducted by domain‑specific evaluation panels (chair + 10–16 members) plus remote experts (used in 2nd stage only). Panels are structured into three scientific domains (LS, PE, SH) and a rotation system of active & shadow panels is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate domain/keywords for your proposal; be aware that remote experts may assess your full proposal in step 2 and that panel composition can affect evaluation perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel selection, keywords, and reviewer exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants choose panel(s) and keywords (panel titles/subtitles/descriptors do not reflect funding priorities). Applicants may name up to 3 potential reviewers to be excluded in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the most appropriate panel and keywords strategically; use reviewer exclusion to avoid obvious conflicts but provide valid reasons if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel capacity limit for Step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a limit of up to 44 proposals per panel in Step 2 of StG, CoG, AdG (replacing the previous budget multiplier rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that even highly rated proposals face panel capacity constraints; emphasise distinctiveness and top quality to increase chances of being within the panel's Step 2 allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A‑score at Step 1 and its implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of a new A‑score at Step 1 with categories: 'A invited' → high quality proposals to pass to Step 2; 'A not invited' → high quality proposals exceeding the threshold for Step 2, but not subject to resubmission restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand Step 1 scoring semantics; an 'A not invited' indicates a high quality assessment but not advancement due to capacity—use reviewer feedback to strengthen future submissions where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission restrictions based on prior call participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for eligibility based on prior participation: If PI participated in 2022 with result C → not eligible in 2024 (StG, CoG, AdG). If PI participated in 2023 with result B or C → not eligible in 2024 (StG, CoG, AdG). If PI participated in 2023 with result A or B → eligible in 2024 (StG, CoG, AdG). Additionally, applicants preparing a grant agreement in a 2023 ERC call may not apply to 2024 ERC calls (StG, CoG, AdG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check past participation results and any ongoing grant agreement preparations to determine eligibility for the 2024 calls before preparing an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lump‑sum funding pilot model (Advanced Grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot lump sum funding model for the Advanced Grant: lump sum contribution for the entire project (defined upfront, 80% pre‑financing); payment based on completion of activities (not on successful outcome); possibility of additional funding and grant portability to be continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying to Advanced Grant calls under the pilot, plan project milestones and reporting aligned to activity completion; budgeting and justification differ from unit‑cost reimbursement models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required and recommended supporting documents & resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant documents include the ERC Work Programme, Standard application form, Information for Applicants, ERC Rules for Submission and Evaluation, ERC Guide for Peer Reviewers, Letter of Commitment of the Host Institution, online submission system guidance, and funded projects & statistics. ERC instructional videos and other resources are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the listed documents and guidance early during proposal preparation; use the Guide for Peer Reviewers to understand assessment expectations and align your proposal accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal preparation timeline and expected time to funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicative timeline from submission to funding is approximately 12–14 months, with specific call open dates, deadlines, dates for information to applicants (1st and 2nd stage), and planned grant agreement signature windows provided per call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposal work and institutional approvals with the full timeline in mind; allow time for eligibility checks, panel processes, interviews, and grant preparation for a realistic project start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel and domain novelties (panel descriptors and scope updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: New panel SH8 (Studies of Cultures and Arts) combining cultural studies, art history, architecture, music, performing arts, museum studies, cultural heritage and other fields with social anthropology. LS3 relabeled to include both stem cell and regeneration biology; LS5 subtitle changed to cover neuroscience in humans and other organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map your proposal to the updated panel descriptors; if your topic sits at boundaries, consider which panel will best appreciate the work and choose keywords accordingly.
